record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: What composite objective functions should be optimized when tuning federated learning systems that must trade off model quality, throughput, convergence speed, fairness, privacy, robustness, and resource use, and how can those settings be tuned automatically rather than manually?

evidence.quote: Deﬁning reasonable composite objective functions, and designing algorithms to automatically tune these settings, has not been explored yet in the context of federated learning systems and hence remains a topic of future research.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a federated learning system in which a central coordinator orchestrates training of a shared model across a large population of distributed clients. The performance of such a system can be characterized by multiple, often competing, criteria, including: (i) model quality Q (e.g., validation accuracy or loss), (ii) throughput T (e.g., updates processed per unit time), (iii) convergence speed C (e.g., wall-clock time or rounds to reach a target quality), (iv) fairness F across clients (e.g., variance of per-client performance, or worst-client utility), (v) a privacy guarantee P (e.g., the (ε, δ) parameters of a differential-privacy mechanism, or a bound on information leakage), (vi) robustness R against adversarial or Byzantine clients and against client drift, and (vii) resource use U (communication bandwidth, on-device compute, energy). Each of these is itself a function of a vector θ of tunable system parameters (number of clients sampled per round, local epochs, learning rates, batch sizes, compression and quantization levels, noise multipliers, aggregation rules, secure-aggregation thresholds, dropout-tolerance settings, etc.).

Formalize and solve the following:

1. Design a family of composite objective functions Φ(θ) = Φ(Q(θ), T(θ), C(θ), F(θ), P(θ), R(θ), U(θ)) suitable for use as optimization targets when tuning a federated learning system, such that Φ encodes principled trade-offs among the seven criteria above and admits meaningful Pareto analysis.

2. Provide algorithms that, given only black-box (and noisy) access to the criteria via system runs or simulations, automatically select θ to optimize Φ — replacing manual tuning — and prove guarantees on their sample complexity, regret, or convergence to (approximate) Pareto-optimal configurations under appropriate assumptions on the criteria as functions of θ.

The task is to produce both the principled construction of Φ and the accompanying automatic-tuning algorithms with formal guarantees.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is an open-ended research direction in federated learning systems. Surveys and follow-up works through 2024–2025 still describe automated multi-objective tuning of FL systems (balancing accuracy, communication, privacy, fairness, robustness) as an active and unresolved area, with various partial heuristics (Bayesian optimization, multi-objective NAS, AutoFL) but no general principled composite objective or tuning algorithm with guarantees.

status_evidence.title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Defining reasonable composite objective functions, and designing algorithms to automatically tune these settings, has not been explored yet in the context of federated learning systems and hence remains a topic of future research.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as unexplored future research in the canonical FL open-problems reference.
